name: Storemapper
tagline: Embeddable store locator that shows shoppers where to buy a brand's products
team: Solo founder for most of its life; a small part-time team near the 2017 sale
summary: Storemapper is a store locator widget for brands that sell through retailers. It embeds on Shopify, BigCommerce, WordPress, Squarespace and other sites. Tyler Tringas taught himself to code, built the first version on a long flight, grew it while traveling, and sold it to SureSwift Capital in July 2017. It is the case he later used to coin the term 'micro-SaaS'.
origin: Tringas spent about nine months learning to code, then built Storemapper's first version on a single long flight to Argentina. He charged $5/mo because the first version was buggy, and had paying customers within about 24 hours.
howItMakesMoney: Monthly subscriptions. It started at $5/mo, and he raised the price 80% to $9/mo for new customers once the product matured, then raised it further in later years. The early low price is his own documented lesson in underpricing.
growth: Platform app stores. Listing on Shopify's app store and building integrations for BigCommerce, WordPress and Squarespace put it in front of merchants on fast-growing platforms.
A viral footer. The 'powered by Storemapper' link on nearly every customer's locator produced thousands of clicks a month.
Organic search for 'store locator' terms. He never ran paid ads.
Repeated price increases on new customers raised ARPU without adding more customers.
moat: A small but real set of integrations across ecommerce platforms and embedded widgets that are annoying to replace. The niche was too small for large companies to target.
risks: Platform dependence: Shopify can ship a native locator or change app-store rules. Competing plugins are cheap, and a low-ARPU product with churn needs constant new customers.

timeline.event: Builds the first version on a flight to Argentina and gets paying customers within about a day at $5/mo
Publishes 'bootstrapped to $50,000/year in 2 years' with live metrics
Publishes '2015 Roadmap: 100K to 4HWW' about getting to $100K ARR on a four-hour week
Indie Hackers interview: ~$21K/mo, driven by targeting the right niche
Sold to SureSwift Capital for an undisclosed 'level up money' price after meeting buyers at MicroConf

lessons: Build on top of a fast-growing platform's app store. Its growth becomes your distribution.
Ship embedded products with a 'powered by' link so every customer markets for you.
Don't anchor on your launch price. Raise it for new customers once the product works.
A narrow utility can support a traveling solo founder and still be sellable to a SaaS holding company.

rebuild.idea: A 'find our product near you' locator for craft breweries, wineries and specialty food brands that ingests messy distributor depletion reports (CSV/Excel) and keeps retailer locations up to date automatically.
rebuild.why: Generic store locators assume the brand keeps a clean store list. Beverage and food brands selling through distributors get irregular spreadsheets, so their 'where to buy' pages go stale.
mvp: Collect 5 real distributor reports from brewery owners and write a parser that normalizes and geocodes accounts
Ship an embeddable map widget with Shopify and WordPress snippets
Charge $29/mo with a monthly 'upload your report' email and auto-refresh
Sell directly to 20 local breweries via Instagram DMs and state brewers' guild forums
rebuild.fit: A data engineer who enjoys messy spreadsheet ETL and geocoding
